scoring_justification: Energy barrier, trend, nucleation shear, and hysteresis pressures can be validated by directly parsing the agent's CSV artifacts and comparing to paper-reported values.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported barrier values (33.19, 18.11, 3.31 meV/atom) and trend of decreasing barrier with increasing lattice parameter.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Phys. Rev. Materials 4, 063609 (2020) Fig.3 and Sec.III A.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual numbers the paper claims as results of DFT calculations; they are used as reference targets with tolerance.

outputs.description: Minimum-energy path data for the dislocation-free bcc-to-hcp transformation at three lattice parameters. The checker will recompute the energy barrier and verify its magnitude, trend, and maximum shift against a hidden reference.

Stepwise shear-induced transformation data with dislocations. The checker will verify that hcp nucleation occurs at a shear value lower than the dislocation-free case, with hcp_fraction > 0.1 for s < 0.27.

Pressure-volume hysteresis data for the pressure-induced transformation cycle with dislocations. The checker will verify forward transformation onset pressure between 80-100 GPa and reverse onset between 110-130 GPa.

output_contract.notes: The dislocation-free MEP data must cover a0 = 3.592, 3.786, 4.110 bohrs. The shear transformation data is for forward direction only at a0=3.592 bohrs. The pressure hysteresis covers a full forward-reverse cycle.

steps.description: Recompute energy barriers for each a0, check within 20% of paper values and decreasing trend.
Check hcp fraction exceeds 0.1 for s<0.30 and final fraction >0.8.
Forward onset 80-100 GPa, reverse onset 110-130 GPa, hysteresis >10 GPa.
